_comment: Driving power-ups (Drifting, Decisions, 'Driving power-ups', board 2026-10-31). The six are the board's (the fifth, the Polarized Steering Wheel: board 2026-11-02, Drifting, Decisions, 'Rusty Paintjob and the Polarized Steering Wheel'; the sixth, Grinding Wheels, one tier: board 2026-11-08, T-586); every tier number is a proposal (Driving & Drift's call by the docs, written on its behalf by Game Data) for the board's playtest. Tier 1 is what the gift gives; tier 2 is the 'next tier' offer and the last. T-520 (Drifting, Decisions, 'Two tiers and three slots for the driving power-ups', board 2026-11-03, the 4-minute run): every power-up has 2 tiers, tier 2 equal to the old tier 4 (the old tiers 2 and 3 are gone). Distances in units (1 unit = the car's width), times in seconds.

offer_when_exhausted.reason: When every power-up is at its last tier there is nothing to offer: the gift is skipped (no overlay, no pause) and the run goes on. An overlay with no choices would only interrupt the run.

tiers.reason: Slow to charge, a short clear burst, so the first tier shows the idea.
Top tier: a big boost any time, still shorter than the hype boost chain.

charge.reason: The charged jump (T-590, a playtest; the board, 2026-11-08, Drifting, Decisions, 'A charged jump, for a playtest'): holding Space on the ground charges the hop, linearly from x1 to x1.5 the tier's takeoff_speed over 3 s (the board's numbers), the hop comes when Space is let go; a tap hops at x1. The same at both tiers: tier 1's 5 becomes 7.5 at full charge (about 1.25 s in the air, 2.25 times the peak), tier 2's 8 becomes 12. Tweak 1 (the board, 2026-11-08): no charge bar; while the charge grows the car tilts as it does in the air (the grind overhaul's 3 frames into the held pose), and the jump effect scales with the jump's height (rail_grind.json, jump_effect_height_exponent).

tiers.reason: A small hop: about 0.83 s in the air with the car's gravity (12), enough for the airtime missions. No cooldown (T-551; the board, 2026-11-07, Drifting, Decisions, "Jump has no cooldown"): a press on the ground always hops.
Long enough for an air 360 (about 1.33 s in the air). No cooldown at this tier either (T-551): tier 2 keeps only its higher takeoff.
T-540: about 1.5 times the old 1.4, so the wall bounce is clearly further than before (2.1 times the plain T-435 bounce).
T-540: 1.5 times the old 2.6; top tier, walls act like springs (3.9 times the plain bounce, still away from the wall, never into it).

Half a minion's health (4, T-408); open questions for the board: the per-enemy repeat cooldown (0.5 s here, so driving through a crowd does not melt it each frame) and whether the kaiju is hit (not at tier 1).
Top tier also scrapes the kaiju (open question for the board).

T-603 (Drifting, Decisions, 'The Polarized Steering Wheel bursts after an alternate drift', board 2026-11-08): each ALT DRIFT! the trick system pays, on the ground and outside the cooldown, multiplies the car's velocity along its travel (whichever way the nose points) by 1.1, the board's half of the old +20%. Held 0.5 s (the board's), then fade_seconds 0.25 (a proposal): the factor falls back to 1 in a straight line, so the car ends at exactly the speed it would have had. 0.25 s is half the hold: quick enough that the burst reads as a kick that ends, not a slow coast-down, and long enough that the drop (about 1.6 units/s at top speed) is no jolt The cooldown (T-527, 3 s) and the shock stay as they were. The old trigger's numbers (min_angle_degrees, max_coast_seconds, min_speed) are gone with the trigger.

T-603: x1.225, the board's half of the old +45% (the card shows +23%, the board's rounding, 2026-11-08), held 0.5 s, faded in 0.25 s as tier 1. Bricks' tier 1 wave at the car on every burst (shock_bricks_tier 1: radius 4, damage 6, minions pushed 4, the kaiju damaged and never pushed, read from weapons.json so it follows Bricks), owned or not. Cooldown 4 s (T-527): longer than tier 1's because the bigger multiplier gains more speed per burst.

grinding_wheels._comment: T-586 (Drifting, Decisions, 'Grinding Wheels, a driving power-up', board 2026-11-08; how it behaves: Drifting, Content, 'Grinding Wheels (task T-586)'), read by scripts/driving/grinding_wheels.gd. One tier for now (the board: a second tier only if it asks), so its card shows the descriptions text (screen_texts.json, T-585) and it has no 'next tier' offer. spark_colours are RGB 0-255, four shades per heat, drawn at random per spark like the plain sparks; none is Greenbull's yellow (247, 208, 52; Visual style, rule 6).

spark_colours.reason: The board's yellow, orange and red (Drifting, Decisions); the shades are the Driving & Drift Agent's proposal: four per heat, a pale hot core down to a deep shade, like the plain sparks' four (rail_sparks.gd). Outside the tiers so the power-up card's number slots (power_up_screen.gd) only see numbers.

tiers.reason: The board's: one stack per full second of the grind, 3 at most (3 s), +100% launch speed at 3 stacks; the per-stack +33% (1, 1.33, 1.67, 2x) is the Project Lead's proposal, written here as max_launch_boost spread over max_stacks so 3 stacks give exactly 2x. The boost multiplies the launch speed after its floor (rail_grind.json launch_min_speed 6): max(grind speed, 6) x (1 + stacks/3), so even the slowest grind held 3 s launches at 12, and the floor keeps a 0-stack launch exactly as without the power-up. No cap on top: a fast grind can launch past top speed (33) and slows back on the ground like any boost. colour_fade_seconds 0.25: each colour holds while its stack holds and fades to the next over the first quarter second of the new stack, so the colour change lands with the stack it shows (a fade spread over the whole second would read as orange-ish yellow before the stack is earned).
